name: Nivolumab
mechanism: Fully human IgG4 monoclonal antibody against PD-1 that prevents PD-L1/PD-L2 engagement, used alone, with ipilimumab or with chemotherapy, including in the perioperative setting.
keyToxicities: Endocrinopathies (thyroiditis/hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, autoimmune type 1 diabetes)
Immune-mediated dermatitis, including rare severe cutaneous reactions
Myocarditis, myositis and myasthenia-like syndromes (rare, potentially fatal)
monitoring: Baseline and periodic thyroid function, liver function, renal function and glucose
Clinical assessment for new respiratory, gastrointestinal, cutaneous, neurological or cardiac symptoms; low threshold for imaging and specialist input
Cortisol and pituitary axis assessment when symptoms suggest hypophysitis or adrenal insufficiency
Troponin and ECG if myocarditis is suspected
interactions: A subcutaneous formulation has been developed.
resistance: Primary resistance is associated with low tumour immunogenicity, STK11/KEAP1 co-mutations and oncogene-driven NSCLC; acquired resistance involves loss of antigen presentation (B2M/HLA loss), JAK1/2 loss-of-function and immunosuppressive microenvironment changes.
